population_detail: children treated with antibiotics for any reason
tier_rationale: Szajewska & Kolodziej 2015 SR (Aliment Pharmacol Ther), 11 RCTs pooled overall (n=1308, RR 0.49 [0.29-0.83], low-quality GRADE); significance is driven entirely by the children subgroup (5 RCTs, n=445, RR 0.48 [0.26-0.89], moderate-quality GRADE) - adults alone were not significant (6 RCTs, n=863, RR 0.48 [0.20-1.15], low-quality), except a Helicobacter pylori-eradication antibiotic subset (4 RCTs, n=280, RR 0.26 [0.11-0.59]). Row scoped to children per tier rule 5; the adult null and H. pylori-subset finding are noted here rather than built as separate rows, since no dedicated adult-only SR exists to grade them from.

health_impact: shortens acute infectious diarrhea in children
effect_size: MD -0.85 day [-1.15, -0.56] duration of diarrhea (SR, 15 of 18 trials pooled for this outcome)
tier_rationale: Szajewska et al. 2019 update SR, 18 RCTs (n=4208); stool volume showed no effect, duration of diarrhea was reduced (15 RCTs, n=3820). The review's own abstract flags 'high heterogeneity and methodological limitations of the included trials', which caps this at tier C by definition regardless of the large pooled N. A recent large RCT (NEJM, ~943 children) included in this pooling found no benefit, driving consistency to mixed; effect was stronger in European cohorts and at doses >=10^10 CFU/day.
dose: 10^9-10^12 CFU/day across pooled trials; >=10^10 CFU/day showed greater effect

effect_size: trend toward reduced incidence, not significant (p=0.08); pooled RR not reported for the LGG subgroup
tier_rationale: McFarland 2007 SR pooled 12 trials of various probiotics for traveler's diarrhea (overall sRR 0.85 [0.79-0.91]); LGG's own subgroup (6 RCTs, 9 treatment arms) reached only a non-significant trend (p=0.08). A null result is as much a finding as a positive one and this is a formal strain-specific subgroup of an SR, so it is graded rather than excluded - but the subgroup's own RR/CI was not reported, only a p-value, which is why this stays at B instead of A.

population_detail: mostly children with IBS (4 of 5 RCTs pediatric; diagnostic criteria varied by trial)
effect_size: significant reduction in abdominal pain severity, I2=25.9% (SR of 5 LGG-only RCTs; pooled RR/MD not reported in abstract)
tier_rationale: Maslennikov et al. 2026 strain-specific SR (single-strain LGG-vs-placebo RCTs only), RoB2-assessed. Pain was the only outcome poolable for LGG - 'other IBS symptoms and quality of life indicators could not be meta-analyzed'. The pooled benefit is fragile: it was lost across all subgroups when trials were stratified by IBS diagnostic criteria, and the dose-response was non-monotonic (benefit only at ~6x10^9 CFU/day, not at 2x10^10 or 4x10^10). Modest pooled N and that inconsistency cap this at B rather than A.
dose: 6x10^9 CFU/day (effect not replicated at 2x10^10 or 4x10^10 CFU/day in the same pool)
duration: 8 weeks (effect not seen at 4 or 6 weeks)
notes: roster_source's shorthand cites this SR under gi-ibs-global; the outcome it actually grades is abdominal pain, so the claim is filed under gi-ibs-pain. Other IBS symptoms and QoL were not poolable for this strain.

tier_rationale: Liu et al. 2024 SR, Cochrane RoB2 tool. Modest pooled N (168) across only 4 trials, and at least one included trial (~4.5x10^9 CFU/day, 4 weeks) reported crying time comparable to placebo while others found large reductions - that inconsistency and the small pool cap this at B. Secondary marker: fecal calprotectin also fell (MD -103.28 ug/g [-149.30, -7.26]).

health_impact: prevents necrotizing enterocolitis in preterm infants
effect_size: RR 0.50 [0.26, 0.93], p=0.03, NEC >=Stage II (SR of 5 LGG-only RCTs)
tier_rationale: Ananthan et al. 2024 strain-specific SR (Cochrane methodology), RCT-only pooled estimate for LGG as sole probiotic. The RR is real but close to the null (CI upper bound 0.93) on only 5 trials. Consistency is marked mixed because a separate single-center before/after cohort (outside this SR) found NEC incidence rose after routine LGG adoption (10.2% to 16.8%), and rare LGG sepsis has been reported in preterm infants specifically - a genuine real-world caution alongside the RCT-level benefit. That tension, not the RCT evidence alone, is why this caps at B rather than A.
safety_flags: A conflicting single-center observational cohort found higher NEC incidence after routine LGG use in a NICU; rare LGG sepsis has been reported in preterm infants. See safety-bacteremia in safety.json.

health_impact: reduces upper respiratory tract infection incidence
effect_size: RR 0.62 [0.50-0.78] for upper respiratory infections (SR, 4 RCTs); RR 0.73 [0.57-0.92] in the >1yr subgroup for overall respiratory infections
tier_rationale: Liu et al. 2013 SR/meta-analysis (Indian Pediatr), 4 RCTs, n=1805. Also reduced antibiotic use (RR 0.80 [0.71-0.91]) and, in the closely related otitis media outcome, incidence (RR 0.76 [0.64-0.91], NNT 17) - since reconciled into the vocabulary as imm-otitis-media-incidence, see gaps. The abstract does not state that risk of bias was formally appraised with a named tool, so this stays at B rather than A per tier rule 4. The composite 'overall respiratory infections' endpoint (all ages) was not significant; only the URTI-specific and >1yr subgroup results were.
dose: 1.3x10^7-2.6x10^7 CFU/day in the largest pooled trial (fermented milk); doses in the other 3 pooled trials not confirmed
duration: 7 months in the largest pooled trial

population_detail: critically ill adults on mechanical ventilation (ICU)
effect_size: PROSPECT (n=2653): HR 1.03 [0.87-1.22], P=.73, no difference in VAP; earlier Morrow et al. 2010 pilot (n=146) found benefit (19.1% vs 40.0% VAP, P=.007), not replicated at scale
tier_rationale: PROSPECT (Johnstone et al. 2021, JAMA), a large multicentre RCT across 44 ICUs, found no VAP benefit and no difference in mortality, ICU length of stay, C. difficile, or antibiotic use, superseding an earlier small single-center pilot (Morrow et al. 2010) that had found a large benefit. No SR pools the two; direction taken from the larger, more recent, better-powered trial per source policy, with the conflict recorded as 'conflicting' rather than silently dropping the earlier finding. This is not a thin literature - PROSPECT alone is adequately powered - but the disagreement between trials and lack of formal bias appraisal caps it at C.
dose: 1x10^10 CFU twice daily (PROSPECT, enteral); Morrow 2010 dose not stated in abstract
safety_flags: PROSPECT found L. rhamnosus recovered from a normally sterile site in 15/1318 (1.1%) probiotic-group patients vs 1/1332 (0.1%) controls. See safety-bacteremia in safety.json.

population_detail: children and young adults with allergic rhinitis (birch-pollen and house-dust-mite sensitized)
effect_size: no significant reduction in nasal, lung, or eye symptoms in either trial versus placebo (numeric effect sizes not reported in the available abstracts)
tier_rationale: Two independent double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs, both null: Helin et al. 2002 (n=36, birch-pollen allergic teenagers/young adults, ATCC 53103, 5.5 months) and a 2013 Indian Pediatrics trial (n=240, house-dust-mite-sensitized children, 3 months). No SR pools them, so bias_assessment stays not_assessed, but 2 independent consistent-direction RCTs without an SR is exactly tier B's definition.

population_detail: middle-aged/older adults without type 2 diabetes (HbA1c trajectory, not treatment of existing diabetes)
effect_size: HbA1c stable on LGG vs increased on placebo over 90 days, F(1,90)=8.44, p=0.005
tier_rationale: Single double-blind RCT (n=93 after exclusions from 200 enrolled), 90 days, no SR available. Scoped per tier rule 5 to the non-diabetic population it actually studied - a separate, smaller RCT in women with existing type 2 diabetes (n=34, 8 weeks, same 10x10^9 CFU/day dose) found no between-group difference in fasting glucose, so this finding should not be read as evidence LGG treats diagnosed diabetes. A single unreplicated RCT without formal bias appraisal caps this at B.
notes: A separate RCT in women with existing type 2 diabetes (DOI:10.1007/s00394-023-03139-3, n=34) found no fasting-glucose benefit at the same dose. Not built as a second row - same impact_id/population pair - see tier_rationale.

effect_size: reduced anxiety-like behavior on open-field testing in both studies (Neufeld 2019 P=0.01; Faucher 2022 P<0.03, active LGG arm only)
tier_rationale: Juvale & Arulsamy 2025 SYRCLE-assessed SR of animal rhamnosus-anxiety studies separates results by strain; 2 of its 15 studies used GG specifically (Neufeld et al. 2019, maternal-separation rats; Faucher et al. 2022, C57BL/6 mice), both anxiolytic on open-field testing. The review's own comparison notes JB-1 (a different rhamnosus strain, not this roster entity) was the most consistent performer across the wider literature (7/8 studies) - GG's own evidence is smaller, though consistent within it. Faucher 2022 also tested heat-inactivated LGG, which did not replicate the effect; this entity is the live preparation, so that arm is noted but not built as a separate row. Tier is P by definition for animal rows; n_studies and consistency carry the strength signal.

population_detail: adults 52-75 with baseline objective cognitive impairment
effect_size: greater improvement in NIH Toolbox Total Cognition Score vs placebo, in the cognitively-impaired subgroup only
tier_rationale: Sanborn et al. 2020 double-blind RCT, n=200 community-dwelling adults 52-75, 3 months. The benefit was confined to participants with objective baseline cognitive impairment; no effect emerged in cognitively intact participants. Scoped per tier rule 5 to the subgroup where the effect actually holds. Single unreplicated RCT, no SR, caps at B.
notes: A separately published human trial testing cognition and stress markers in young men used strain JB-1, not GG, and is excluded here - see gaps.

population_detail: newborn Wistar rats, gliadin-induced enteropathy model; C57BL/6J mice, DSS-induced colitis model
effect_size: co-administration with gliadin challenge restored villus length (+53.5% vs gliadin-alone, P<0.05) and upregulated tight-junction/adhesion genes (ZO-1 18.1-fold, occludin 10.9-fold, beta-catenin 6.9-fold, E-cadherin 8.3-fold by qPCR; beta-catenin +590.6% and E-cadherin +39.9% by Western blot, both P<0.05) versus gliadin alone (Orlando et al.); separately, GG restored occludin expression and reduced fecal/serum IL-6 (P=0.049 / P=0.040) in a DSS-colitis mouse model via upregulated arginine metabolism (Lin et al. 2025)
tier_rationale: Preclinical, tier P by definition. Both studies confirmed strain GG (ATCC 53103) and used a barrier-injury challenge model (gliadin enteropathy; DSS colitis) rather than healthy-animal baseline, so the finding is specifically about barrier restoration under insult, not baseline barrier enhancement. A frequently cited Journal of Dairy Science tight-junction study (ZO-1/MLCK upregulation) was excluded after verification showed it used a different Lactobacillus rhamnosus strain, OLL2838, not GG - see gaps.
dose: 1x10^9 CFU/day x10 days (Orlando); 10^8 CFU single gavage (Lin)

population_detail: hospitalized adult VRE carriers on antibiotics; formula-fed infants with colic
effect_size: no significant alpha-diversity difference vs placebo in hospitalized adults (Krishna et al., n=10 LGG/11 placebo microbiome subset, richness p=0.148-0.713, Shannon p=0.078-0.813; beta-diversity difference P=0.006 attributed to baseline imbalance, not treatment); in infants, alpha diversity was significantly LOWER in the LGG arm than control (P=0.022) and beta diversity differed at study end (P=0.05), though LGG's own relative abundance was higher in that arm (P<0.001) (Cohen-Silver et al., n=35/36)
tier_rationale: Two independent RCTs, both strain-confirmed GG, in very different populations, without a pooling SR - B per the multiple-independent-RCT rule. Consistency marked mixed rather than conflicting: neither trial found LGG improves overall microbiome diversity, but the direction in infants (significantly lower alpha diversity on LGG) is a genuine negative signal beyond simple nulls, worth surfacing rather than averaging away. GG's own detectable abundance rising in both settings shows the strain is present and active without translating into a diversity benefit.
dose: 60x10^9 CFU/day (adults, 4 weeks); dose in infant formula not stated in abstract (3 weeks)
notes: The adult trial's primary endpoint (VRE eradication) was also null - 57% LGG vs 56% placebo cleared at 4 weeks - consistent with the absence of a broader microbiome effect.

population_detail: human Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cell monolayers
effect_size: Salmonella Typhimurium adhesion reduced from ~16.4% to ~9.5% under thermal-stress conditions (P=0.001) and cytotoxicity reduced from 30.5% to ~7.3% (P=0.001), Caco-2 model; separate studies show competitive exclusion/displacement of E. coli and Salmonella spp. from Caco-2 cells and intestinal mucus via steric hindrance, strain-dependent in degree
tier_rationale: Preclinical/in vitro row, tier P by definition. Confirmed strain GG (ATCC 53103) in both the quantified Salmonella thermal-stress study (Caco-2, PMID:19542213-family literature) and the broader Collado-group competitive-exclusion/mucus-adhesion literature. GG showed no protective effect on unstressed Caco-2 cells - the significant reduction in pathogen adhesion and cytotoxicity was specific to epithelial cells under thermal stress, a detail kept in effect_size rather than smoothed over.
notes: A separately reported 75.7% adhesion reduction and 41.7% invasion inhibition of E. coli used primary chicken intestinal epithelial cells rather than a human model - directionally consistent but not pooled into effect_size above since it is a different (avian) system.

health_impact: transiently or persistently colonizes the gut
population_detail: healthy adults, single-arm colonization studies (no placebo comparator)
effect_size: recovered from colonic biopsies in 4 of 5 subjects after 12 days of consumption (Alander 1997); detectable in feces and biopsies for over a week after discontinuation (Alander 1999)
tier_rationale: Two small uncontrolled human studies from the same research group (Alander et al. 1997, n=5 colonoscopy patients; Alander et al. 1999, n=5 volunteers), both using a whey drink fermented with confirmed strain GG, identified by colony morphology, lactose fermentation, and PCR. No control arm and no comparator strain in either study, so this is descriptive colonization data, not a controlled effect - tier D per uncontrolled human observational evidence. The finding itself (GG attaches to colonic mucosa and persists transiently rather than permanently colonizing) is consistent across both studies.
dose: ~6x10^10 CFU/day (Alander 1999; dose not confirmed for the 1997 biopsy study)
duration: 12 days consumption; detectable >1 week after discontinuation
notes: Both studies note fecal sampling alone understates colonization - mucosal biopsy was needed to detect GG in some subjects fecal-negative at that timepoint.

population_detail: patients with a compromised gut barrier or indwelling central line: immunocompromised/immunosuppressed patients (including active IBD on corticosteroids), short-bowel-syndrome infants, preterm/NICU infants, and critically ill adults with central venous catheters
effect_size: not applicable - case reports have no denominator; genomic/molecular strain typing (WGS, PFGE, or 16S rRNA sequencing) confirmed the bloodstream isolate matched the ingested probiotic strain GG in every case cited here
tier_rationale: Human safety signals of this kind live almost entirely in case reports per source policy, so tier D applies by definition regardless of how many cases exist or how tightly strain identity is confirmed. Five independent, molecularly strain-confirmed cases across four independent publications plus a strain-specific SR's safety note: (1) an immunocompetent trauma patient with a central venous catheter and GI compromise, WGS-confirmed, cleared without antibiotics; (2) an infant with short bowel syndrome, PFGE-confirmed; (3) an adult with severe active ulcerative colitis on corticosteroids, 16S-confirmed, with concurrent candidemia; (4) a pediatric ulcerative-colitis patient, 16S-confirmed, recovered after 5 days of antibiotics; (5) rare sepsis noted in preterm infants in the strain-specific NEC-prevention SR (see gi.json's gi-nec-prevention). Every identified case involves a host-side barrier or line vulnerability, not bacteremia in an otherwise healthy oral consumer - that pattern, not the raw case count, is what independently_replicated:yes and consistency:consistent are tracking here.
notes: Related but not pooled into this row: PROSPECT (a large ICU RCT, see imm-vap in immune.json) found L. rhamnosus recovered from a normally sterile site in 15/1318 (1.1%) probiotic-group ICU patients vs 1/1332 (0.1%) controls - a sterile-site-culture signal in critically ill adults, not a bacteremia case series, but consistent with the same compromised-barrier risk pattern. A single-center NICU cohort also found higher necrotizing enterocolitis incidence after routine LGG adoption (see gi-nec-prevention) - NEC itself is a different outcome from bacteremia, but the two safety signals co-occur in the same preterm population and both argue for caution in NICU use specifically. Several additional L. rhamnosus bacteremia case reports exist in the literature (renal transplant, burn patient, recurrent bacteremia/endocarditis, splenic hematoma) but were excluded here because the reports available did not confirm strain GG specifically versus another L. rhamnosus strain or an unidentified commercial product - per the taxonomy trap discipline, species-level 'L. rhamnosus' case reports are not treated as GG-specific evidence.
